ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A bicycle wheel of mass $M=2.8 \mathrm{~kg}$ and radius $R=0.3 \mathrm{~m}$ is spinning with angular velocity $\omega=5 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ around its axis in outer space, and its center is motionless. Assume that it has all of its mass uniformly concentrated on the rim. A long, massless axle is attached to its center, extending out along its axis. A ball of mass $m=1.0 \mathrm{~kg}$ moves at velocity $v=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ parallel to the plane of the wheel and hits the axle at a distance $h=0.5 \mathrm{~m}$ from the center of the wheel. Assume that the collision is elastic and instantaneous, and that the ball's trajectory (before and after the collision) lies on a straight line.

<image_1>

Find the time it takes for the axle to return to its original orientation. Answer in seconds and round to three significant figures.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the bicycle wheel is drawn as a vertical circular/elliptical rim, and the axle extends horizontally to the right along the symmetry axis of the wheel; on the left side of the wheel there is a rotation-direction arrow labeled omega; on the right-side axle, the distance h from the wheel center to the collision point is marked; a gray small ball is at the lower right, with velocity arrow v vertically upward, indicating that the small ball collides in a straight line with the axle at a point a distance h from the wheel center. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take the collision impulse J in the direction of motion of the small ball. The wheel is a thin hoop, so the moment of inertia about the axle is I3 = M R^2 = 2.8 * 0.3^2 = 0.252 kg m^2, and the moment of inertia about any transverse diameter is I1 = I3/2 = 0.126 kg m^2. The effective velocity of the collision point in the impulse direction is J/M + h^2 J/I1, and the speed of the small ball after the collision is v' = v - J/m. Elastic collision makes the relative velocity reverse: v' - (J/M + h^2 J/I1) = -v, therefore J = 2v/(1/m + 1/M + h^2/I1). Substituting m=1.0, M=2.8, h=0.5, I1=0.126, v=2 gives J = 4/(1 + 1/2.8 + 0.25/0.126) = 1.197 N s. The transverse angular momentum given to the wheel by the impulse is L_perp = hJ = 0.5986 kg m^2/s; the original spin angular momentum is L_spin = I3 omega = 0.252 * 5 = 1.26 kg m^2/s. The magnitude of the total angular momentum is L = sqrt(L_spin^2 + L_perp^2) = sqrt(1.26^2 + 0.5986^2) = 1.395 kg m^2/s. In a symmetric gyroscope with no external torque, the precession angular velocity of the axle about the fixed total angular momentum is L/I1, so the period for the axle to return to its original direction is T = 2*pi*I1/L = 2*pi*0.126/1.395 = 0.5675 s, which to three significant figures is 0.568 s.

method.method_draft: Use an impulse/effective-mass collision calculation followed by torque-free symmetric-top precession. First read the diagram as showing the wheel’s symmetry axis/axle extending horizontally, the ball moving upward along a straight line to hit the axle at offset h from the wheel center, and the wheel initially spinning about the axle with angular speed omega. From the text take M=2.8 kg, R=0.3 m, omega=5 rad/s, m=1.0 kg, v=2 m/s, h=0.5 m, elastic instantaneous collision, and rim mass distribution. For a hoop, use I3=MR^2 about the axle and I1=I3/2 about any transverse diameter. Let J be the collision impulse along the ball’s line. The struck point on the free wheel has post-impact velocity J/M + h^2 J/I1 along the impact direction, while the ball has v' = v - J/m. Elasticity gives reversal of relative velocity: v' - (J/M+h^2J/I1) = -v, so J = 2v/(1/m+1/M+h^2/I1). The impulse gives a transverse angular momentum L_perp=hJ, while the original spin angular momentum remains L_spin=I3 omega along the axle. The conserved total angular momentum magnitude is L=sqrt(L_spin^2+L_perp^2). For a torque-free symmetric top, the axle unit vector precesses about fixed L with angular speed L/I1, so the return time to the original orientation is T=2*pi*I1/L. Substituting the numbers gives T≈0.568 s.

method.method_draft: Use global conservation laws to solve the post-collision state, then use Poinsot/free-top geometry. From the image identify the axle as the wheel’s spin axis, the ball’s line of motion as perpendicular to the axle at the labeled offset h, and the impact as producing a transverse rotation of the wheel while leaving the spin about the axle unchanged. From the text take the masses, radius, speeds, elastic condition, and straight-line path. Define the final ball speed u along the same line, the wheel center-of-mass speed V along that line, and the wheel’s new transverse angular speed beta. Use I3=MR^2 and I1=MR^2/2. Write conservation equations for the collision after subtracting the unchanged spin energy: linear momentum m v = m u + M V; angular momentum about the wheel center in the transverse direction m v h = m u h + I1 beta; kinetic energy (elastic) (1/2)m v^2 = (1/2)m u^2 + (1/2)M V^2 + (1/2)I1 beta^2. Solve these three equations for u,V,beta; equivalently delta=v-u satisfies delta=2v/(1+m/M+m h^2/I1), and L_perp=I1 beta=m h delta. Combine this with the unchanged axial spin L_spin=I3 omega to obtain |L|=sqrt(L_spin^2+L_perp^2). In torque-free motion of an axisymmetric body, the axle maintains a fixed cone around the conserved L vector and completes one cone revolution in time T=2*pi I1/|L|. Evaluate and round to three significant figures to get 0.568 s.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The attached schematic shows a bicycle wheel drawn as a rim with spokes, with a horizontal axle passing through the wheel center and extending outward along the wheel’s spin axis. The wheel has an indicated spin angular velocity ω. A ball is shown below and to the right, moving upward along a straight line labeled v. Its line of motion is perpendicular to the axle and offset from the wheel center by a labeled distance h along the axle. Thus the impact is on the axle at distance h from the center, producing angular momentum transverse to the original spin axis while the original spin about the axle remains unchanged.

Reasoning: For a thin rim wheel, the moment of inertia about the axle is I3 = M R^2, and about any transverse diameter is I1 = M R^2 / 2. With M = 2.8 kg and R = 0.3 m, I3 = 2.8(0.3)^2 = 0.252 kg m^2 and I1 = 0.126 kg m^2. The original spin angular momentum is L_spin = I3 ω = 0.252(5) = 1.26 kg m^2/s.

Let the ball’s final speed along the same straight line be u, the wheel center speed be V, and the induced transverse angular speed be β. Subtracting the unchanged spin energy, use conservation of linear momentum, angular momentum about the wheel center in the transverse direction, and kinetic energy:
1) m v = m u + M V
2) m v h = m u h + I1 β
3) (1/2)m v^2 = (1/2)m u^2 + (1/2)M V^2 + (1/2)I1 β^2.
Equivalently, with δ = v - u, δ = 2v / (1 + m/M + m h^2/I1). Substituting m = 1.0 kg, v = 2 m/s, h = 0.5 m, M = 2.8 kg, and I1 = 0.126 kg m^2 gives δ = 4 / (1 + 1/2.8 + 0.25/0.126) = 1.19715 m/s. Therefore the transverse angular momentum imparted to the wheel is L_perp = I1 β = m h δ = 1(0.5)(1.19715) = 0.598575 kg m^2/s.

The total conserved angular momentum magnitude after collision is |L| = sqrt(L_spin^2 + L_perp^2) = sqrt(1.26^2 + 0.598575^2) = 1.39495 kg m^2/s. For torque-free motion of an axisymmetric body, the axle precesses around the fixed angular momentum vector with period T = 2π I1 / |L|. Hence T = 2π(0.126) / 1.39495 = 0.5675 s, which rounds to three significant figures as 0.568 s.

Subtracting the unchanged spin energy, use conservation of linear momentum, angular momentum about the wheel center in the transverse direction, and kinetic energy:
1) m v = m u + M V
2) m v h = m u h + I1 β
3) (1/2)m v^2 = (1/2)m u^2 + (1/2)M V^2 + (1/2)I1 β^2.
Equivalently, with δ = v - u, δ = 2v / (1 + m/M + m h^2/I1). Substituting m = 1.0 kg, v = 2 m/s, h = 0.5 m, M = 2.8 kg, and I1 = 0.126 kg m^2 gives δ = 4 / (1 + 1/2.8 + 0.25/0.126) = 1.19715 m/s. Therefore the transverse angular momentum imparted to the wheel is L_perp = I1 β = m h δ = 1(0.5)(1.19715) = 0.598575 kg m^2/s.

The total conserved angular momentum magnitude after collision is |L| = sqrt(L_spin^2 + L_perp^2) = sqrt(1.26^2 + 0.598575^2) = 1.39495 kg m^2/s. For torque-free motion of an axisymmetric body, the axle precesses around the fixed angular momentum vector with period T = 2π I1 / |L|. Hence T = 2π(0.126) / 1.39495 = 0.5675 s, which rounds to three significant figures as 0.568 s.

raw_record.original_question:
A bicycle wheel of mass $M=2.8 \mathrm{~kg}$ and radius $R=0.3 \mathrm{~m}$ is spinning with angular velocity $\omega=5 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ around its axis in outer space, and its center is motionless. Assume that it has all of its mass uniformly concentrated on the rim. A long, massless axle is attached to its center, extending out along its axis. A ball of mass $m=1.0 \mathrm{~kg}$ moves at velocity $v=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ parallel to the plane of the wheel and hits the axle at a distance $h=0.5 \mathrm{~m}$ from the center of the wheel. Assume that the collision is elastic and instantaneous, and that the ball's trajectory (before and after the collision) lies on a straight line.

Find the time it takes for the axle to return to its original orientation. Answer in seconds and round to three significant figures.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the bicycle wheel is drawn as a vertical circular/elliptical rim, and the axle extends horizontally to the right along the symmetry axis of the wheel; on the left side of the wheel there is a rotation-direction arrow labeled omega; on the right-side axle, the distance h from the wheel center to the collision point is marked; a gray small ball is at the lower right, with velocity arrow v vertically upward, indicating that the small ball collides in a straight line with the axle at a point a distance h from the wheel center. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take the collision impulse J in the direction of motion of the small ball. The wheel is a thin hoop, so the moment of inertia about the axle is I3 = M R^2 = 2.8 * 0.3^2 = 0.252 kg m^2, and the moment of inertia about any transverse diameter is I1 = I3/2 = 0.126 kg m^2. The effective velocity of the collision point in the impulse direction is J/M + h^2 J/I1, and the speed of the small ball after the collision is v' = v - J/m. Elastic collision makes the relative velocity reverse: v' - (J/M + h^2 J/I1) = -v, therefore J = 2v/(1/m + 1/M + h^2/I1). Substituting m=1.0, M=2.8, h=0.5, I1=0.126, v=2 gives J = 4/(1 + 1/2.8 + 0.25/0.126) = 1.197 N s. The transverse angular momentum given to the wheel by the impulse is L_perp = hJ = 0.5986 kg m^2/s; the original spin angular momentum is L_spin = I3 omega = 0.252 * 5 = 1.26 kg m^2/s. The magnitude of the total angular momentum is L = sqrt(L_spin^2 + L_perp^2) = sqrt(1.26^2 + 0.5986^2) = 1.395 kg m^2/s. In a symmetric gyroscope with no external torque, the precession angular velocity of the axle about the fixed total angular momentum is L/I1, so the period for the axle to return to its original direction is T = 2*pi*I1/L = 2*pi*0.126/1.395 = 0.5675 s, which to three significant figures is 0.568 s.
